Throwing for user validation errors.
realWorldExample: Production apps combine error.tsx boundaries with Sentry via instrumentation.
interviewTip: Clearly separate expected vs unexpected errors.

quiz.prompt: How should a Server Action report a validation error?
options: Return an error value in its result
quiz.explanation: Return expected errors so the form can show them.

title: Production Architecture
description: Organize a large Next.js codebase for teams, performance and security.

sections.title: Layers
sections.content:
- **Routes (`app/`):** thin pages and layouts composing features.
- **Features:** UI + Server Actions per domain (`features/billing`).
- **Data Access Layer:** server-only functions with auth checks, caching and DTOs.
- **Shared UI:** design system components.
- **Infrastructure:** db client, auth, logging, config validation.

sections.title: Decisions to document
sections.content:
- Which data is cached, for how long, and how it's invalidated (tags).
- Where auth is checked.
- When to use Server Actions vs Route Handlers.
- Client state approach for complex interactions.

sections.title: Scaling teams
sections.content: Monorepos (Turborepo, Nx) share packages across apps; Multi-Zones can split one domain across several Next.js apps.

codeExamples.title: Feature-oriented layout
codeExamples.code:
src/
  app/
    (marketing)/...
    (app)/dashboard/page.tsx      # composes features
  features/
    billing/
      components/InvoiceTable.tsx
      actions.ts                  # 'use server'
      queries.ts                  # server-only, cached
  lib/
    db.ts  auth.ts  env.ts
  components/ui/
codeExamples.explanation: Pages stay thin, features own their logic, and data access is centralized and secured.

commonMistakes: Business logic inside page components.
No documented caching strategy, causing stale data bugs.
realWorldExample: Large e-commerce teams use monorepos with shared UI packages and multiple Next.js apps.
interviewTip: For architecture questions, talk in layers and trade-offs.

quiz.prompt: Where should authorization checks for data reads live?
quiz.explanation: Check close to the data.

flashcards.front: Tool to split one domain across several Next.js apps?

title: Testing Next.js Apps
description: Combine unit, component and end-to-end tests for App Router projects.

sections.title: What to use
sections.content:
- **Unit tests (Vitest/Jest):** utilities, validation schemas, data functions, Server Action logic (call them like functions with mocked dependencies).
- **Component tests (RTL):** Client Components and synchronous Server Components.
- **E2E (Playwright/Cypress):** async Server Components, routing, auth flows, caching behaviour against a production build.

sections.title: Tips
sections.content: Run E2E against `next build && next start` for realistic behaviour. Mock network with MSW in unit and component tests.

codeExamples.title: A Playwright test
codeExamples.explanation: The test exercises the full stack: Server Component rendering, Server Action mutation and revalidation.

commonMistakes: Trying to unit test async Server Components with RTL.
Running E2E only against the dev server.
realWorldExample: CI pipelines run Vitest on every push and Playwright on preview deployments.
interviewTip: Explain why async Server Components are covered by E2E tests.

quiz.prompt: End-to-end tests are the recommended way to test async Server Components today.
quiz.explanation: Unit testing tools don't fully support them yet.

flashcards.back: A production build (next build && next start).

title: Monitoring & Observability
description: Know what's happening in production with instrumentation, logs and Web Vitals.

sections.title: Tools
sections.content:
- `instrumentation.ts` with `register()` to initialize tracing (OpenTelemetry via `@vercel/otel`) and `onRequestError` to capture errors.
- `instrumentation-client.ts` for client-side monitoring setup.
- `useReportWebVitals` to send LCP, INP and CLS from real users.
- `after()` from `next/server` to run logging or analytics after the response is sent.

sections.title: What to watch
sections.content: Error rates, slow routes, cache hit rates, Web Vitals by page, and failed Server Actions.

codeExamples.title: Logging after the response
codeExamples.explanation: The client gets the response immediately; analytics runs afterwards without slowing the request.

commonMistakes: Blocking responses on analytics calls.
No visibility into server errors in production.
realWorldExample: Teams export OpenTelemetry traces to Datadog or Honeycomb to find slow data fetches.
interviewTip: Mention instrumentation, after(), and real-user metrics.

quiz.prompt: What does after() do?
options: Schedules work after the response is sent
quiz.explanation: after() runs once the response has finished.

title: Next.js Best Practices
description: A compact summary of modern App Router best practices.

sections.title: Rendering & data
sections.content:
- Default to Server Components; add 'use client' at the leaves.
- Fetch data where it's used; run requests in parallel.
- Be explicit about caching; tag and revalidate after mutations.
- Stream slow UI with Suspense and `loading.tsx`.

sections.title: Mutations & security
sections.content:
- Use Server Actions for UI mutations; validate input and authorize inside every action.
- Keep a server-only Data Access Layer returning DTOs.
- Don't depend on proxy alone for auth.

sections.title: Performance & quality
sections.content:
- `next/image`, `next/font`, `next/script` with lazy strategies.
- Enable the React Compiler; analyze bundles.
- TypeScript strict, ESLint, tests in CI, monitoring with instrumentation.
- Follow release notes: Next.js 15 made APIs async and caching opt-in; Next.js 16 introduced Cache Components, Turbopack by default and proxy.ts.

codeExamples.title: Typed page with async params
codeExamples.explanation: Generated route types catch typos in params at compile time.

commonMistakes: Following Next.js 13/14 tutorials that assume cached fetch and synchronous params.
Turning everything into Client Components to avoid learning boundaries.
realWorldExample: High-performing teams keep a living checklist like this in their engineering handbook.
interviewTip: When asked for best practices, group them: rendering, data, security, performance, tooling.

quiz.prompt: Following a Next.js 13 tutorial exactly guarantees correct behaviour in Next.js 16.
quiz.explanation: Caching defaults, async APIs and middleware naming have changed.

flashcards.back: Async request APIs (params, cookies) and caching opt-in by default.
